jobs.description: About this opportunity: At Freenome, you will help develop the assay technologies used to analyze patient samples and contribute to our mission of early detection and intervention in human disease. As a Research Associate I/II, you will provide experience in next-generation-sequencing (NGS)-based analyses of DNA. Starting with a prototype assay, you will contribute to developing and validating clinical-grade assays to measure complex, blood-based analytes. You will work closely with multiple teams including molecular research, computational science, automation engineering, and clinical operations to develop the assays in a regulated, high-throughput environment as well as identify ways to rapidly iterate and improve on existing methods to evaluate technologies that can enhance our end-to-end test performance. The role reports to the Senior Manager and Staff Research Scientist. This role will be an Onsite role. What you’ll do: Apply knowledge of molecular biology, nucleic-acid biochemistry, and next-generation sequencing to develop assays for DNA. Characterize automated assays by generating and analyzing experimental data. Gather high-quality data, take detailed notes, and openly communicate on lessons learned while performing experiments. Collaborate with research team and computational biologists, understand how data reflect underlying molecular biology, and contribute to analyzing data and generating study conclusions. Present data in cross functional teams. Participate in troubleshooting efforts and design experiments with some supervisor guidance. Help with process improvements across the lab by thinking critically about the execution of all experiments. Must haves: Bachelors with 1+ years of relevant industry experience or Masters in molecular biology, or a related field. Hands-on experience in NGS based assay development including sample preparation, library preparation, target capture, and sequencing. Biological understanding of human cell-free nucleic acids, single-cell analysis methods, immunology, and/or cancer biology. High attention to detail and ability to record accurate and detailed observations, assess impact, and perform troubleshooting as required. Flexible and highly motivated to learn new skills and comfortable adapting to changing priorities. Ability to manual pipette with high confidence, accuracy, and precision. Clear and proactive communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively with team members in the same and adjacent disciplines. Nice to haves: Experience working in a regulated laboratory environment (CLIA, GLP/GCLP, IVD development). Experience with automated platforms in plate-based, low-volume formats and/or microfluidics and experience working with automated liquid handlers. Experience using ELN (electronic lab notebook) and LIMS (lab information management system). Familiarity with programing in a scientific programming language (e.g., Python or R). jobs.title: Research Engineer, Benchmarks & Evaluation
jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT RAMP LABS Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 70,000+ companies use to move money. We think the defensible part of an AI product is the loop: proprietary environments, evals that track what customers care about, and models trained against both. ABOUT THE ROLE Every model decision at Ramp Labs runs through a benchmark. Which model to route to. Whether a post-training run worked. Whether an agent is ready to post a corrective journal entry to a customer's ledger without a human in the loop. You'll own Ramp's benchmarking effort. You'll turn real finance work (expense policy review, invoice coding, month-end close, spreadsheet Q&A) into benchmarks and RL environments, build the graders, and tell the team what is actually improving. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Build benchmarks from real workflows: turn agent traces, customer edge cases and expert labels into versioned benchmark suites for long-horizon agents that run for hours across tools and systems, plus tool use, multi-step reasoning and financial judgment - Own the benchmarking effort: decide what we measure, run benchmark suites across models and agent versions, and report results the team makes decisions on - Design graders: rubrics, programmatic checks and llm-as-judge, calibrated against human agreement, with a clear view of where each one breaks - Close the loop with post-training: turn evals into reward functions and RL environments, and catch reward hacking and contamination before they ship - Publish external benchmarks and write-ups on how models perform at real finance work WHAT YOU NEED - Hands-on experience building LLM benchmarks or evals that people used to make real decisions - Strong Python and software engineering; your eval code is reproducible and fast - Statistical judgment: variance, confidence intervals, sample size, inter-rater agreement, and knowing when a delta is noise - Working knowledge of post-training (SFT, RL with verifiable rewards) and how evals feed into it - Comfort with SQL and large datasets; you'll work directly from production traces - Taste for what is worth measuring NICE-TO-HAVE - Industry experience on an eval, benchmarking or post-training team - Built RL environments or verifiers for agentic tasks - Published benchmark or evaluation research (NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, ICML, ACL) - Built or contributed to eval frameworks (verifiers, lm-evaluation-harness, HELM or similar) - Familiarity with accounting, finance or other expert-domain work - Public work we can look at: a benchmark, an eval suite, a failure-analysis write-up BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL) - Flexible PTO - Centralized home-office equipment ordering - Health and wellness stipend - Budget for intra-office travel - Weekly coffee stipend UNITED STATES - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents - One Medical annual membership - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay - Pet insurance - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed) CANADA - Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life - Life, AD&D, and disability coverage - Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime) - Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP) - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay - Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health UNITED KINGDOM - Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite - Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi - Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay REFERRAL INSTRUCTIONS If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Agent Auth
jobs.description: About Vercel: Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience. Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide. About the role Agents are becoming first-class users of the internet. They sign in, call APIs, deploy code, and act on behalf of people and teams. That raises questions the web was never designed to answer: Who is this agent? Who does it work for? What is it allowed to do, for how long, and how do we know? As an engineer on the [ Agent Auth and Identity ] team, you'll help answer those questions. You'll build the systems that let agents and people authenticate, delegate access, and act safely across Vercel and the services our customers connect to. This is foundational work: identity and authorization sit underneath everything we ship, and getting them right for agents will shape how modern software gets built. The scope is intentionally broad. You might spend one quarter designing how credentials are issued and scoped for autonomous agents, and the next building the developer-facing APIs and SDKs that make secure auth feel effortless. You'll own systems end-to-end, from design through long-term operation in production. We're looking for engineers who care deeply about security and developer experience in equal measure, enjoy working on problems without established playbooks, and want to define how trust works in an agentic world. What you'll do Design, build, and operate the identity, authentication, and authorization systems that power Vercel and our Customers for both people and agents. Shape how agents prove who they are, act on behalf of users and teams, and receive scoped, time-bound, auditable access. Build secure, scalable APIs, services, and SDKs that make auth simple for developers and their agents to adopt. Work with modern and emerging standards (such as OAuth 2.x, OIDC, and agent-focused protocols) and help influence where they go next. Lead projects end-to-end: identify opportunities, set technical direction, and deliver improvements in security, reliability, and developer experience. Partner closely with product, security, and platform teams across Vercel to make identity a strength of every product we ship. Participate in the on-call rotation, taking responsibility for the reliability of critical systems. Contribute to open source and the broader community conversation on agent identity and trust. Write clean, efficient, tested, and well-documented code that others can build upon confidently. What you need [3+] years of experience designing, building, and operating backend systems in production at scale. Strong proficiency in JavaScript/TypeScript, or a comparable backend language and the willingness to work primarily in TypeScript. Solid understanding of authentication and authorization concepts, such as sessions, tokens, OAuth/OIDC flows, permission models, and secrets management. A security-minded approach to engineering: you think about threat models, least privilege, and failure modes as part of design, not as an afterthought. A track record of end-to-end ownership, from design and implementation through to long-term operation. Ability to reason about architectural tradeoffs, balancing long-term vision with pragmatic delivery. Strong cross-team collaboration skills and the ability to drive alignment toward shared goals. Curiosity and comfort working in a fast-moving space where the right answers are still being figured out. Bonus if you Have built or operated identity providers, auth platforms, or access-control systems used by other developers. Have experience with delegated authorization, workload identity, service-to-service auth, or machine credentials. Have worked on LLM-powered agents, tool calling, or protocols like MCP. Have experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform). Are familiar with React or Next.js. Have contributed to open-source projects or standards bodies. Benefits & Compensation Competitive compensation package, including equity. Inclusive Healthcare Package. Learn and Grow: we provide mentorship and send you to events that help you build your network and skills. Flexible Time Off. We will provide you the gear you need to do your role, and a WFH budget for you to outfit your space as needed. The base pay range for this role is $196,000 – $294,000. Actual salary will be based on job-related skills, experience, and location. The total compensation package may include benefits, equity-based compensation, and eligibility for a company bonus or variable pay program depending on the role. Your recruiter can share more details during the hiring process. Disclosures: Privacy: Please review our Job Applicant Privacy Policy for more information on how we handle your data. Equal Opportunity: Vercel is committed to fostering and empowering an inclusive community within our organization. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Vercel encourages everyone to apply for our available positions, even if they don't necessarily check every box on the job description.

Responsibilities include cultivating and maintaining key relationships and working with customers and internal partners that enable Signatera patient retention and unit growth within existing customers. Analyze and monitor patient testing to ensure that patients remain on the protocol prescribed by the Oncologist. Assess the needs of medical professionals and staff members with a focus on customer support, coordination of logistics, and problem solving Become experts on all Natera Oncology products and processes to maximize effectiveness in the field. Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Clinical Oncology Specialist opportunity with Natera at Natera.

Best,
Celina Lin

Robinhood has gone all-in on an AI-accelerated workforce: every week, Hoodies across Finance, HR, Legal, Compliance, and beyond use sanctioned AI tools to build working prototypes of the tools they wish they had. The best of those ideas deserve to become real software. That is this team's entire job, and yours. The team is built on the premise that AI multiplies what a senior engineer can own: agents do the first pass of assessment, porting, and scaffolding; you review, harden, and decide. The work is a distinctive loop. A prototype earns real usage in our experimental sandbox and arrives through a single front door. You assess it, decide what survives, often the idea and the workflow, rarely the code, and rebuild it as an enterprise-grade, production-spec service that meets our full engineering standards: SSO, audit logging, secrets management, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, and security review, baked in from the first commit. While you build, you work directly with business partners, the forward-deployed pattern, pointed inward. Robinhood operates in a heavily regulated industry. Building fast here means building safely, and this team exists to help make sure those aren't in tension. This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Demonstrated AI-native development: daily fluency with agentic coding tools, experience building LLM-powered applications or agentic workflows, and the judgment to review, harden, and productionize AI-generated code. Product sense and scoping discipline: you can find the 20% of a prototype worth keeping, say no to the rest, and finish, this team's leverage depends on engagements that end. jobs.title: Organ Health Specialist
jobs.description: TERRITORY: Northern California (Sacramento to Eureka and Redding) and Northern Nevada (Reno, Carson City, and surrounding communities). We are looking for an Organ Health Specialist (OHS) to join the Organ Health sales team! In this role, you will drive growth and market development within the general nephrology market by cultivating new and maintaining existing key relationships, executing strategic business plans, and promoting the adoption of Organ Health products. Your expertise and insights will play a critical role in advancing our mission to support healthcare providers with innovative diagnostic tools. RESPONSIBILITIES As an Organ Health Specialist , you will promote and sell Renasight , a genetic test analyzing 385 genes to identify potential hereditary causes of kidney disease, and Prospera , a non-invasive cfDNA test for early detection of kidney transplant rejection—both supporting comprehensive kidney health management from diagnosis to post-transplant care. Achieve and exceed performance goals through effective sales strategies, client relationship building, and territory management. Drive market adoption of Natera’s Organ Health portfolio (Renasight and Prospera), contributing to successful product launches and market expansion. Serve as a local expert on Natera’s technology and services, representing the company with professionalism and technical expertise. Develop and execute tailored local business plans to achieve sales objectives and maximize available resources. QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent educational background. A minimum of 3-5 years of progressive sales experience, ideally within laboratory, molecular, or diagnostic sales. Proven track record of closing sales, building client relationships, and driving revenue growth. Proven ability to drive adoption through clinical education and consultative selling Existing relationships with key opinion leaders (KOLs) in nephrology or specialty medicine. Knowledge of academic medical systems and large hospital systems (IDNs) related to nephrology or specialty medicine. Travel up to 50% - 75% within territory, with 10% - 20% overnight stay KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES Proven ability to collaborate with diverse teams to define and execute strategic plans effectively. Demonstrates a hunter mentality with a proven track record of successfully growing and managing a territory. Strong problem-solving skills with a creative and independent approach to overcoming challenges. Exceptional interpersonal, presentation, and communication skills, fostering meaningful connections and delivering impactful results. Thrives in dynamic and fast-paced environments, demonstrating initiative, self-motivation, and excellent time management skills. The total On Target Earnings (OTE) offers a competitive base salary and uncapped quarterly commissions. In addition we also offer a car allowance, and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs). Compensation & Total Rewards The compensation package listed is for 1st year OTE, which are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. On-target earnings (OTE) represent the total potential income an employee can earn by achieving 100% of their performance goals. It combines a base salary with commissions and serves as an estimated figure rather than a guaranteed amount, providing a guideline based on average performance outcomes. This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including: Long-term equity awards Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision) 401(k) with company match Generous paid time off and company holidays Additional wellness and work-life benefits Compensation Range $180,000 — $200,000 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com . Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws. If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/ Please be advised that Natera will reach out to candidates with a @ natera.com email domain ONLY. Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team. Natera takes cyber crimes seriously, and will collaborate with law enforcement authorities to prosecute any related cyber crimes. For more information: - BBB announcement on job scams - FBI Cyber Crime resource page

cold_email.subject: Interest in Organ Health Specialist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Organ Health Specialist opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

About the Role In this role, you’ll work within a 5-15k sq ft distribution center, will assist in leading the local warehouse operating team, and in some locations, includes preparing food in a light-prep kitchen, and help the Site Manager ensure we maintain high quality for our customers. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Lead: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your site, helping your team to navigate new initiatives and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners. Operate: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results in one or more specific focus areas or a specific shift for your site. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success through effective scheduling and by executing inventory management processes and deploying best practices from across the network. You’ll engage cross-functional partners as needed for support. Strategize: Within the focus area(s) assigned by your Site Manager, you’ll analyze data and make strategic recommendations and execute actions regarding resource allocation, workflow, warehouse organization and when to engage cross-functional partners. You may also lead some process improvement projects. Delight: We are customer-obsessed. You’ll coach and empower your team to provide a highly quality customer experience with every order. Quality metrics such as order accuracy and fulfillment speed will be key measurements of success for your team. You’ll also work cross-functionally with central teams from our inventory to training teams to ensure your team has the tools and resources they’ll need to deliver. We’re excited about you because… You’re a proven leader. You have managed high-performance teams of 5+ employees with successful performance and employee development outcomes. You relish ownership. You’re excited to have ownership in a new and rapidly growing business. No problem is too big or too small for you, and you’re ready to show up however needed for your team. You solve problems from first principles. You’re excited to solve problems in innovative ways, and you resist “this is how it’s always been done” thinking. You’re unafraid of ambiguity. Rapid change and learning is exciting to you, and you thrive in ambiguous, startup environments. You’re analytical . You let data win arguments. You are a data-first problem solver and you have experience using Excel or Google Sheets to analyze data, including using basic formulas and creating pivot tables. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Connect
jobs.description: About Vercel: Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience. Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide. About the Role Vercel Connect helps developers give agents and AI-built apps secure access to the data, tools, and events they need—without wrestling with OAuth, credentials, and integration complexity. We’re currently building two things: 1) a platform for managing agent identity, access and permissions and 2) a set of rich connectors for the 1000s of systems (like Linear, Slack, GitHub, Google, etc.) that agents will need to talk to. We’re solving core problems like agent identity and delegated access, tool approval and standards around making agents aware of changes on 3rd party platforms. As a senior engineer on this team you'll not only own our APIs, token infrastructure, authorization, SDKs, and more, but work with external companies to make it easier for developers to build agents that integrate with their products. You’ll need to balance both high uptime and fast performance with flexibility to allow for seamless connection to many systems that weren’t designed with agents in mind. If you’re looking for a role that will put you at the center of how agent identity and credentials work, this is it! What You Will Do Ship provider integrations end to end — auth flows, token exchange, app registration, and the configuration UI — from generic API-key and OAuth presets through bespoke cases like Snowflake Partner Connect, Slack manager apps, and Microsoft Entra. Own and improve our infrastructure (uptime, performance, secure storage of credentials and keys) and developer experience for Connect Work with industry leaders within and outside of Vercel to propose and implement new authentication and authorization protocols for AI era Build and harden event forwarding — signature verification inbound, project-scoped identity outbound, delivered to the right deployment and environment. Make Connect the obvious way to give an agent a credential, extending the SDKs , consent-redirect flow, and framework adapters. Reduce the cost of the next hundred integrations, so most new providers become configuration rather than code. Work directly with the teams building on Connect, and turn what you learn into platform improvements. About You 6+ years building and operating production backend or full-stack systems, with a track record of owning a service or platform surface rather than a feature. You deeply understand your users problems and work in a focused manner to address them, leveling up the product you’re working on over time. Deep, practical understanding of OAuth 2.0/2.1, OIDC, and JWTs — not just wiring up a client library, but reasoning about authorization codes, PKCE, refresh semantics, audience and scope restriction, token exchange, and what each of those actually protects against. A security instinct for integration code specifically — SSRF and DNS rebinding, confused-deputy and mix-up attacks, redirect-URI validation, webhook signature verification, tenant isolation. You've either found these bugs or fixed them. Strong TypeScript , and comfort developing backend and frontend components. Experience integrating with many third-party APIs , an appetite for the reality of it — undocumented behavior, non-compliant OAuth, inconsistent errors — and the judgment to absorb that mess behind a clean abstraction. You're comfortable with ambiguity, ship incrementally against a large surface, and communicate clearly with the teams building on top of you. You push the envelope of leveraging agents and AI in ur dev workflow, giving you the insight to help build the agent platform of the future Bonus Points You've built or operated an OAuth authorization server , an identity provider, or a multi-tenant integrations platform. Experience with MCP , agent tool-calling, or delegated-access and consent patterns. Prior work on integration marketplaces, partner engineering, or webhook infrastructure at scale. Open source contributions, particularly in the auth, Next.js, or agent tooling ecosystems. Compensation & Benefits: Competitive compensation package, including equity. Inclusive Healthcare Package. Learn and Grow - we provide mentorship and send you to events that help you build your network and skills. Flexible Time Off. We will provide you the gear you need to do your role, and a WFH budget for you to outfit your space as needed. The San Francisco, CA base pay range for this role is $196,000-$294,000. Actual salary will be based on job-related skills, experience, and location. Compensation outside of San Francisco may be adjusted based on employee location. The total compensation package may include benefits, equity-based compensation, and eligibility for a company bonus or variable pay program depending on the role. Your recruiter can share more details during the hiring process. Disclosures: Privacy: Please review our Job Applicant Privacy Policy for more information on how we handle your data. Equal Opportunity: Vercel is committed to fostering and empowering an inclusive community within our organization. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Vercel encourages everyone to apply for our available positions, even if they don't necessarily check every box on the job description.

jobs.title: Engineer
jobs.description: Career Category Engineering Job Description Position Summary The Engineer – Engineering Technical Authority (ETA) will support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of engineering practices, standards, and processes that enable effective Engineering Project Delivery. This role will work closely with Engineering Technical Authorities, subject matter experts (SMEs), project teams, and global engineering stakeholders to develop and maintain the Engineering Design Library and Engineering Project Delivery framework . A key focus of the position will be translating engineering knowledge, requirements, lessons learned, and industry practices into clear and effective engineering standards, specifications, procedures, SOPs, guidance documents, and tools. The role will also support the organization, governance, accessibility, and lifecycle management of engineering knowledge and controlled documentation. The ideal candidate has an engineering or related technical background, strong technical communication and information-management skills, and a foundational understanding of biotechnology, pharmaceutical manufacturing, or another regulated engineering environment. Key Responsibilities Engineering Technical Authority & Engineering Design Library Support Engineering Technical Authorities and SMEs in the development and maintenance of engineering standards, specifications, design guidelines, and other Engineering Design Library content. Coordinate with engineering disciplines to capture technical requirements and translate SME knowledge into clear, actionable engineering documents without changing technical intent. Review existing engineering documents and identify opportunities for improvement, consolidation, clarification, and standardization. Support periodic review and revision of Design Library documents to incorporate lessons learned, technology changes, industry practices, and evolving business needs. Promote consistency in engineering requirements, terminology, document structure, and application across engineering disciplines and sites. Support governance and lifecycle management of engineering standards, specifications, procedures, and related technical content. Support organization, metadata, searchability, and accessibility of Engineering Design Library content. Engineering Project Delivery Support development and continuous improvement of Engineering Project Delivery processes, procedures, SOPs, guidance documents, templates, and tools. Work with project delivery and engineering SMEs to document effective practices across the project lifecycle. Support development and revision of engineering requirements associated with project planning, design, execution, commissioning, qualification, and turnover. Capture lessons learned from engineering projects and support incorporation of those lessons into engineering standards and project delivery practices. Help identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, and improve engineering processes and project execution. Technical Documentation & Change Management Author and revise engineering standards, specifications, SOPs, procedures, technical guidance, and related engineering documents. Translate complex technical information into clear, concise, and actionable engineering requirements. Facilitate working sessions with SMEs to capture technical knowledge and develop structured engineering content. Coordinate document reviews and work with stakeholders to resolve comments and reach technical alignment. Manage multiple document revisions, reviewers, deadlines, and approval workflows. Support communication of Engineering Standards and Specifications (ESS) changes to affected stakeholders. Develop process maps, workflows, tables, diagrams, and other tools to improve communication of engineering requirements and processes. Research applicable external codes, standards, and industry guidance to support document development. Technical interpretation and ownership of requirements remain with the designated ETA SME. Working Hours & Global Collaboration Model The role should be structured to provide reliable support to U.S., Europe, and Asia stakeholders. The working model may be established as Hybrid . The selected model should preserve protected time for focused document work while providing planned overlap for SME reviews, global meetings, and ESS change communications. Model Work Hours Global Overlap Reference* Recommended Use HYBRID Mon–Thu: 9:30 AM–3:30 PM at site, with split remote work before/after site hours; Fri: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM ET Per AIN reference: 3 hr with PT; 3 hr with ET; 5 hr with EU; 6 hr with Singapore Best when on-site ETA/SME interaction is important while retaining global collaboration flexibility. *Global overlap periods are intended as planning references. Specific meeting windows may vary based on stakeholder location, project needs, and critical SME availability. Skills & Qualifications Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical discipline. Degrees or demonstrated experience in technical communications or information management may also be considered where accompanied by sufficient engineering or technical experience. Experience working with engineering standards, specifications, procedures, technical documentation, or controlled document systems in a regulated or highly structured environment. Strong technical writing, editing, document-control, and information-organization skills. Ability to work effectively with subject matter experts and translate technical inputs into clear, usable document content without changing technical intent. Experience with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, document libraries, metadata/search concepts, and collaboration tools or equivalent engineering knowledge platforms is desirable. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple document revisions, deadlines, reviewers, and approvals simultaneously. Comfort working across global time zones and adjusting meeting windows when critical SME or stakeholder participation is required. Working knowledge of how external codes, standards, and industry guidance influence engineering requirements; the role is expected to coordinate and research, while technical ownership remains with the designated ETA SME. Foundational knowledge of biotechnology, pharmaceutical manufacturing, life sciences, or another regulated manufacturing environment is preferred. Familiarity with engineering drawings, P&IDs, equipment specifications, design documentation, or capital-project engineering deliverables is desirable. Key Competencies Engineering & Technical Understanding – Applies engineering fundamentals and technical knowledge to understand requirements, recognize gaps, and effectively engage the appropriate SMEs. Technical Communication – Translates complex engineering concepts and SME input into clear, concise, and actionable standards, specifications, procedures, and guidance without altering technical intent. Technical Curiosity – Quickly develops an understanding of unfamiliar technologies, systems, engineering disciplines, codes, and standards and asks effective questions to clarify requirements. Knowledge & Information Management – Organizes engineering information so that requirements and technical knowledge are controlled, searchable, accessible, and usable by the engineering community. Collaboration & Facilitation – Builds effective working relationships with Technical Authorities, SMEs, project teams, and global stakeholders and facilitates development and review of technical content. Systems Thinking – Understands how engineering standards, project delivery processes, external requirements, and individual technical requirements interact across the engineering lifecycle. Execution & Organization – Effectively manages multiple documents, stakeholders, reviews, deadlines, and approval workflows while maintaining document quality. Continuous Improvement – Identifies opportunities to simplify, standardize, and improve engineering practices, documentation, knowledge management, and project delivery processes. Role Focus This position serves as an Engineer within the Engineering Technical Authority organization . Strong technical writing, document management, and information-management capabilities are important competencies of the role, but the position is not intended to function as a standalone technical writer. The Engineer will help ETA capture and organize engineering knowledge, maintain the Engineering Design Library, improve Engineering Project Delivery processes, and enable Technical Authorities and SMEs to efficiently develop, maintain, and communicate engineering requirements across the global engineering organization. Technical ownership and approval of discipline-specific engineering requirements remain with the designated Engineering Technical Authority or SME. .

jobs.description: About the Team We're looking for someone to help scale DoorDash's next billion dollar business, DashMart, by growing our in-house food program, DashMart Kitchens. The DashMart Kitchens team is focused on building a new type of restaurant platform within DashMart, offering a broad selection of prepared foods and well-known restaurant staples to our customers' doorsteps. About the Role As the Kitchen Manager for DashMart Kitchens (DMK), you’ll lead the daily operations of a DoorDash-owned kitchen located within a DashMart fulfillment center. You’ll oversee a team of operations associates and shift leads to ensure every meal is prepared safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards. You’ll combine hands-on culinary leadership with operational excellence — managing staffing, scheduling, and kitchen performance while ensuring food safety, order accuracy, and team success. You’ll work closely with your Site Manager to lead multiple food concepts, improve processes, and create a great place to work. In addition to leading the kitchen, you'll be cross trained into DashMart operations and expected to work on both sides of the business. This role requires strict adherence to food safety, inventory controls, and safety protocols due to routine access to food, supplies, equipment, and operational systems. You’re excited about this opportunity because you... Enjoy learning how different parts of a complex operation connect and are excited to collaborate cross-functionally Are passionate about food and love to lead across multiple food concepts Enjoy building processes and seeing ideas come to life Are passionate about creating food consistently Want to grow in delivery-only kitchen operations Thrive in hands-on, fast-paced leadership roles. You’ll Make an Impact By... Leading: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Kitchen Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. Because this position supervises staff and is responsible for maintaining a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, strong adherence to professional conduct and employee safety standards is required. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your DMK, helping your team to navigate new food concepts and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners. Operating: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results for your kitchen. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success through effective scheduling and by ensuring par levels are met, recipes are accurately executed, and best practices from across the network are deployed. Because this role oversees high-risk kitchen equipment and fast-paced food production, maintaining sound judgment and unimpaired performance is essential to ensure a safe work environment. You’ll engage cross-functional partners as needed for support. Strategizing: You will analyze performance metrics, identify root causes of issues like prep gaps or order quality, and implement solutions that drive efficiency and adoption. You will refine processes, and partner with your Site Manager and cross-functional teams to execute new initiatives and continuously improve how the kitchen operates. Delighting: You care deeply about delivering great food and a great customer experience. You will coach your team to maintain recipe accuracy, food safety, and storefront availability, knowing that consistency is key in a multi-concept kitchen. You will collaborate with central teams so your site has the tools, training, and support needed to achieve excellent quality outcomes. We’re excited about you because… You have 3+ years of experience in a medium/high-volume fast-casual or full-service restaurant environment. You have 1+ years of experience leading teams, including hiring, scheduling, coaching, and performance management. You hold (or are willing to get) a ServeSafe Manager certification and set high standards for food safety and cleanliness. You’re a hands-on leader who motivates teams of 5+ employees to perform and grow. You take ownership and thrive in fast-changing, startup-style environments where no task is too big or small. You’re a creative problem solver who challenges “how it’s always been done” and finds better ways forward. You’re analytical, data-driven, and comfortable using Excel or Google Sheets to make decisions. As the leader of the site, you will need to ensure your team and the site is fully supported, which will include regularly scheduled late-night and weekend hours. You’re comfortable flexing between kitchen and fulfillment operations, and you understand how culinary execution and order flow connect to overall site metrics like accuracy, quality, and efficiency. You have (or can quickly learn) a working knowledge of inventory management systems (IMS), product flow, and fulfillment best practices within a multi-operation site. Compensation Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. jobs.title: Creative, Experiments
jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world. This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. Experiments make expression, introspective, optimistic, thoughtful, and impactful things with frontier models. Continuing to experiment while pushing the spectrum of what the voice and stories we tell. We bring creative and technical collaborators together to explore what these models make possible through prototypes, interactive experiences, physical objects, and stories that invite people to participate, reflect, and imagine. About the Opportunity We’re looking for a Creative, Experiments to help develop and make original work for the Experiments program. You’ll contribute to a distinctive body of work with frontier models, finding ideas that connect new capabilities with human curiosity, humor, and everyday life. You’re a creative thinker and a hands-on maker who moves comfortably between storytelling, design, and technology. You can turn an open-ended question into a compelling concept, build a working prototype with creative and technical partners, and carry an idea through iteration and delivery. You’ll contribute ideas to the program’s creative agenda, identify opportunities worth exploring, and work with creative and technical partners to make them real. Working closely with the Experiments Team, you’ll help explore new possibilities for Research Design. The work may take the form of digital experiences, physical installations, playful objects, films, or formats we have yet to discover. Each experiment should have a clear idea, thoughtful execution, and a reason to matter to its audience. This role is based in the US and partners closely with OpenAI’s Creative, Research, Product, Engineering, and Communications teams, alongside external makers and production partners. In this role, you will: - Contribute to the Experiments program’s slate of ideas, owning individual projects from initial exploration through public release in partnership with creative leads - Develop original concepts that use frontier models to make work with humor, emotional depth, optimism, and meaningful impact - Prototype early and often, working hands-on and with creative technologists to test interactions, explore model behavior, and refine the idea - Collaborate across design, storytelling, engineering, and production to create digital and physical experiences with strong craft and a clear point of view - Build relationships with internal teams and external makers, coordinate project needs, and use audience response and project learnings to inform the next experiment You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 8+ years of relevant experience - Bring a portfolio of original experiments, experiences, or creative projects that shows your role in developing ideas, collaborating across disciplines, and making the work - Combine conceptual thinking, experience design, and storytelling with curiosity about technology and a strong sense of humor, culture, and human behavior - Are a resourceful maker who explores frontier models and emerging tools through practical experimentation and can partner effectively with technical specialists - Can take ownership of open-ended projects, use feedback to refine what to pursue, and balance ambitious ideas with practical scope, timelines, and delivery - Work with curiosity and generosity, build trust across disciplines, and contribute to an environment where collaborators take creative risks and learn together - Support your teammates, adapt when experiments don’t go as planned, and iterate and ship quickly About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning. About the Role We’re looking for a Designer to lead hands-on design for research and experimental creative work. You’ll help define a project’s visual direction, build prototypes, and carry promising ideas through to finished work across research communications, demos, and experiences. jobs.title: Maintenance & Reliability (M&R) Engineer
jobs.description: Career Category Engineering Job Description Maintenance & Reliability (M&R) Engineer Job Description Amgen discovers, develops and delivers innovative human therapeutics. A biotechnology pioneer since 1980, Amgen was one of the first companies to realise the new science’s promise by bringing safe, effective medicines from lab, to manufacturing plant, to patient. Amgen therapeutics have changed the practice of medicine, helping millions of people around the world in the fight against cancer, kidney disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and other serious illnesses. With a deep and broad pipeline of potential new medicines, Amgen remains committed to advancing science to dramatically improve people’s lives. Amgen Dun Laoghaire (ADL) is a 37,000 square metre aseptic drug product operations facility, currently undergoing expansion, specialising in secondary manufacturing activities – Formulation, Vial/Syringe Filling, Lyophilisation and Packaging. The ADL site also includes laboratories and cold chain warehouse capabilities. There is a strong culture of continuous improvement and innovation within ADL to strive for solutions that improve health outcomes and dramatically improve people’s lives. Amgen is developing the capability to produce all of its medicines in Dun Laoghaire, helping to ensure continuity of supply of our medicines as we expand internationally. The Maintenance & Reliability (M&R) Engineer is responsible for improving the reliability, availability, and maintainability of plant equipment within the ADL manufacturing facility. The role focuses on developing and sustaining a robust reliability framework that ensures right-first-time maintenance execution, minimises unplanned downtime, and optimises asset lifecycle performance in support of safe, compliant, and efficient operations. The role partners closely with Engineering, Operations, and Quality to analyse equipment performance, identify failure modes, and implement preventive and predictive maintenance strategies. The Maintenance Reliability Engineer also leads continuous improvement initiatives to reduce non-commercial time, improve equipment uptime, and increase overall plant availability. Key Duties and Responsibilities Support Drug Product manufacturing within the Vial and Syringe filling plants. Develop, optimise and modernise the maintenance PMO programme to ensure equipment maintenance is maintained at the right level, frequency while also utilising digital tools to enhance predictability and targeted maintenance strategies. Employ business analytics to assess performance and identify improvement opportunities for Equipment Reliability, Maintenance Reliable Execution, Condition Monitoring and Predictive Maintenance. Develop & Design Multi-Year Reliability roadmap and ensure flawless execution with close collaboration/partnership with key cross-functional stakeholders. Analyse equipment performance data (e.g. downtime, failure trends, MTBF, MTTR) to identify chronic issues and implement sustainable reliability improvements. Collaborate with system owners, planners, and technicians to define maintenance scopes, refine job plans, and ensure maintenance tasks are technically sound, risk-based, and executable. Support shutdown and non-commercial time activities by ensuring reliability-critical work is correctly prioritised, scoped, and executed to deliver right-first-time outcomes. Drive continuous improvement through the cycle, capturing lessons learned and embedding standard work, best practices, and technical documentation into future maintenance execution. Lead and support system improvements, development of detailed specifications, engineering documents and standard operating procedures. Solving complex problems, project management, equipment lifecycle management and operational excellence. Support a safe working environment by complying with all pertinent environmental health/safety practice, rules and regulations. Basic Qualifications • Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Electronic, Chemical, Software) or related scientific discipline and/or relevant experience. • Minimum of 2-3 years’ experience in a GxP manufacturing environment in a maintenance, reliability, or an engineering type role. • Demonstrated ability to work across functional boundaries and influence outcomes without direct authority. Preferred Experience • 2-3 years’ engineering or scientific experience in a pharmaceutical or biotech manufacturing environment. • Proven experience implementing reliability improvement initiatives in complex, multi-system facilities. Knowledge and Relevant Experience • Strong working knowledge of pharmaceutical/biotech manufacturing and aseptic processing. • Fundamental understanding of GxP, EHS, and regulatory compliance requirements. • Asset reliability methodologies (RCA, FMEA, criticality analysis, PM optimisation). • Experience with CMMS/EAM systems and data-driven maintenance decision-making. • Application of continuous improvement tools and methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma, TPM). Skills • Strong collaborator who promotes a culture of reliability, accountability, and continuous improvement. • Ability to assess and influence both short- and long-term decisions impacting equipment uptime and plant availability. • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and prioritisation skills. • Strong technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to clearly convey complex technical concepts to diverse audiences. • Ability to balance tactical execution with strategic reliability planning. What you can expect of us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way. In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers competitive and comprehensive Total Rewards Plans that are aligned with local industry standards. Apply now and make a lasting impact with the Amgen team. careers.amgen.com As an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people around the world, Amgen fosters an inclusive environment of ethical, committed and highly accomplished people who respect each other and live the Amgen values to continue advancing science to serve patients. Together, we compete in the fight against serious disease. Amgen is an Equal Opportunity employer. We make all employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities, consistent with legal requirements. Please contact us to request accommodation. . Salary Range 55,960.60 EUR - 75,711.40 EUR

jobs.description: Career Category Engineering Job Description 1. Position Summary The ESS Specifications, Standards & Guidelines serves as the operational and technical documentation to the Engineering Technical Authority team. This role helps ensure that Engineering Specifications, Standards and Guidelines remain current, internally consistent, easier to find, and better aligned with applicable industry standards and recognized engineering practices. The resource will work closely with ETA subject matter experts (SMEs), document owners, to coordinate document updates, support the development of new ESS documents, maintain search and access capabilities, and cascade changes through the EDL platform and established communications. 2. Key Responsibilities ESS Maintenance & Industry Alignment: Maintain assigned Amgen Engineering Specifications, Standards and Guidelines and coordinate periodic reviews to improve clarity, consistency, usability, and alignment with applicable industry standards and engineering practices. SME Document Revision Support: Provide hands-on support to ETA SMEs during document updates and revisions, including document control coordination, incorporation of SME comments, formatting, reference checking, revision history, review-cycle tracking, and preparation for approval. New ESS Development: Support ETA in the development of new Specifications, Standards and Guidelines by coordinating inputs, facilitating working sessions, organizing source material, and progressing drafts through the established review and approval process. ESS Change Cascade & Communications: Cascade information on new and updated ESS documents to ETA and the broader engineering community through the EDL platform and agreed communication channels. Maintain concise change summaries, effective dates, links to current documents, and communication records. Governance & Coordination: Maintain a practical ESS tracker and review calendar; monitor document status, owners, planned revisions, approvals, and publication; identify overdue or high-priority actions; and provide routine status reporting to ETA leadership. 3. EDL Platform & Communication Support The resource will maintain the operational interface for ESS updates in the EDL environment, including the established "Updated ESS Documents" SharePoint list and related communication process. · Post or coordinate publication of approved ESS changes in accordance with ETA governance. · Prepare short, user-focused update messages covering document title, revision, change summary, effective date, impacted audience, and link to the current version. · Maintain a communication record so ETA can confirm that updates were cascaded to the intended engineering audience. 4. Interfaces & Collaboration Primary interfaces include ETA Technical Authorities and SMEs, Engineering discipline leads, Facilities/Utilities, project engineering teams, Quality/Validation stakeholders as applicable, document owners, and digital/knowledge-management platform support. The resource is expected to work hybrid time zones and maintain a predictable communication rhythm with global stakeholders. 5. Working Hours & Global Collaboration Model The role should be structured to provide reliable support to U.S., Europe, and Asia stakeholders. The working model may be established as Hybrid. The selected model should preserve protected time for focused document work while providing planned overlap for SME reviews, global meetings, and ESS change communications. Model Work Hours Global Overlap Reference* Recommended Use HYBRID Mon-Thu: 9:30 AM-3:30 PM at site, with split remote work before/after site hours; Fri: 9:00 AM-6:00 PM ET Per AIN reference: 3 hr with PT; 3 hr with ET; 5 hr with EU; 6 hr with Singapore Best when on-site ETA/SME interaction is important while retaining global collaboration flexibility. 6. Skills & Qualifications · Bachelor's degree in engineering, technical communications, information management, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience. · Experience working with engineering standards, specifications, procedures, technical documentation, or controlled document systems in a regulated or highly structured environment. · Strong technical writing, editing, document-control, and information-organization skills. · Ability to work effectively with subject matter experts and translate technical inputs into clear, usable document content without changing technical intent. · Experience with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, document libraries, metadata/search concepts, and collaboration tools or equivalent engineering knowledge platforms is desirable. · Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple document revisions, deadlines, reviewers, and approvals simultaneously. · Comfort working across global time zones and adjusting meeting windows when critical SME or stakeholder participation is required. · Working knowledge of how external codes, standards, and industry guidance influence engineering requirements; the role is expected to coordinate and research, while technical ownership remains with the designated ETA SME. 7. Role Boundaries This resource supports the ETA team but does not replace the technical authority of the designated ETA SME or document owner. Technical decisions, interpretations of requirements, approvals, and final release authority remain with the assigned Amgen technical and governance owners. .

jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.description: Career Category Clinical Job Description As a Data Scientist, you will develop statistical, machine-learning and AI models for assigned Clinical Development questions with guidance from experienced colleagues. You will align analyses with study objectives, produce reproducible code and explain assumptions, findings and limitations. You will build pharmaceutical and clinical-data knowledge while using approved tools and methods with appropriate scientific and human review. Responsibilities · Apply statistical, stochastic and forecasting methods to questions involving study design, trial execution and monitoring. · Apply standard ML and AI methods with guidance, comparing results with agreed baselines. · Prepare permitted clinical datasets and document provenance, quality checks and evaluation splits. · Develop reproducible R, Python and SQL code; record model, data and assigned prompt versions. · Run agreed model tests and check AI outputs for errors, unsupported claims and limitations. · Collaborate across regions with Data Science, Clinical Development, Programming, Statistics and data-platform partners. · Test outputs with CfDA, GBS and GDO, seeking human review before clinical use. · Understand end-user analytical needs and improve the usability of analytical outputs. · Prepare reviewed findings, reproducible handoffs, user guidance and training materials. Accountabilities · Deliver reliable analyses and models that support decisions within assigned Clinical Development work. · Protect sensitive data, use approved AI services and escalate unsafe or unreliable outputs. · Contribute reusable analyses, evaluation cases, modeling components and documented workflows. · Take ownership of agreed deliverables while escalating risks, assumptions and limitations. · Maintain the quality, reproducibility and usability of code and outputs. · Deliver validated analyses, models and documentation on time. · Recommend modeling approaches and make code, testing and documentation decisions within agreed standards. Basic Qualifications · 5-9 over all experience · Bachelor’s degree and 2 years of related experience or Master’s degree Preferred Qualifications · Master’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Operations Research, Computer Science or another scientific or technical discipline. · Internship or early-career experience in the pharmaceutical or high-tech industry. · Strong capability in R and/or Python, with familiarity with SQL and data manipulation. · Familiarity with reproducible workflows, version control, testing and documentation. · Experience with statistical, simulation, forecasting or ML methods, with exposure to AI evaluation where relevant. · Basic ML and generative AI literacy and the ability to learn approved tools with review. · Working knowledge of statistical modeling, uncertainty, model validation and interpretation. · Understanding of Clinical Development, or the ability to build this knowledge quickly. · Ability to recognize AI errors, privacy risks and limits of use when handling permitted clinical data. · Learning agility, quantitative reasoning, accountability and effective cross-functional communication. .

cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Manager, Marketing Operations opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. Best,

jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. The Senior Manager, Digital & Process Excellence is responsible for leading process excellence and digital transformation initiatives across Global Supply Chain (GSC). This role owns the development, governance, and continuous improvement of business process management, process intelligence, automation, and digital enablement capabilities that support operational excellence and organizational effectiveness. Working closely with business teams, BIT, and other enabling functions, the role translates business needs into scalable solutions, operating models, and capability roadmaps. Responsibilities include leading transformation initiatives, establishing governance frameworks, advancing process intelligence and automation capabilities, and ensuring adoption of new processes, tools, and ways of working across the organization. The ideal candidate combines expertise in business process management, digital technologies, and organizational transformation with strong leadership, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills. This individual must be comfortable influencing across organizational boundaries, navigating ambiguity, and driving complex initiatives that deliver measurable value. Key Responsibilities The Sr Process Manager is responsible for owning and supporting a wide portfolio driven by business needs that encompass the following activities at varying degrees of depth and engagement. Own the strategy, governance, and continuous improvement of Global Supply Chain business process management capabilities, standards, and operating models. Own the design, governance, and lifecycle management of enterprise process architectures and process models using BPM methodologies and approved process management platforms. Own the delivery, adoption, and value realization of digital and process transformation initiatives across Global Supply Chain. Own governance frameworks, intake processes, lifecycle controls, and quality standards that enable sustainable process excellence across GSC. Identify, evaluate, and deploy opportunities to leverage automation, analytics, process intelligence, AI-enabled capabilities, and emerging technologies to improve operational effectiveness and business performance. Build and scale digital enablement capabilities, including learning resources, knowledge management assets, AI-enabled solutions, and adoption programs that increase organizational capability and effectiveness. Own performance measurement and value realization frameworks, including adoption metrics, maturity indicators, business outcomes, and continuous improvement opportunities. Partners with business teams, BIT, and other enabling functions to translate business needs into scalable solutions, enterprise capabilities, and strategic roadmaps. Lead change management, stakeholder engagement, communications, and capability-building activities that support enterprise adoption of new processes, tools, and ways of working. Lead cross-functional initiatives involving stakeholders across GSC, GPS, BIT, and other enterprise functions spanning multiple geographies and time zones. Stay current on industry trends and leading practices in business process management, process intelligence, process mining, automation, AI, and continuous improvement, incorporating relevant advancements into GSC capabilities and roadmaps. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor’s degree in Business, Data Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. 7+ years of experience in business process management, supply chain operations, digital transformation, continuous improvement, or related disciplines; life sciences or pharmaceutical experience preferred. Experience establishing and sustaining process governance frameworks, standards, controls, and lifecycle management practices. Strong digital, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate emerging technologies and identify opportunities to improve business performance. Experience leading changes, driving adoption, and enabling large-scale transformation initiatives through stakeholder engagement, training, and communications. Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, Design Thinking, or other continuous improvement methodologies is a plus.
